Today's verdict BULLISH-OPPORTUNISTIC
When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index 1/10: 1-2 signals, price action quiet vs Mother Jaws 100/100: maximum divergence composite, 15 bearish pairs vs 4 bullish across 40 pairs
These measure different things on different timescales. The Crash Index captures realized price dislocations already underway. Mother Jaws measures how far cross-asset correlations have broken from their historical norms, which leads price. Trust Mother Jaws for where prices are going; the Crash Index tells you only that you haven't arrived yet.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score 76: STRONG BUY, capitulation signal vs Regime bias RISK-OFF: 3 risk-off signals aligned, regime score 42 in TRANSITION
Extreme fear in the contrarian signal is consistent with a risk-off regime: the selling creates the sentiment extreme. Use the contrarian score to gauge how much of the decline is sentiment-driven, not as a standalone buy trigger. The regime direction takes precedence for positioning.
Today's tension
A capitulation-level contrarian buy at 76 sits inside a risk-off transition regime, and both readings are telling you something true
Bull

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The regime sits at 42 (TRANSITION) with 3 risk-off signals aligned. That combination is a clear directional lean: pare gross exposure, raise cash, and wait for the regime to clear above 50. A contrarian score of 76 tells you fear is at capitulation levels, but fear in a transition regime confirms the selling is happening, not that it has stopped.

The internal picture is more damaged than the S&P level suggests. SPY and its equal-weight version have drifted from a correlation of +0.52 to -0.18: mega-cap is holding the index while the average stock gets sold. KOSPI dropped -4.4% over five days, the Russell 2000 dropped -3.0%, and the S&P itself is down only -1.1%. The macro regime reads INFLATIONARY at just 30% confidence, meaning the system cannot commit to a playbook. Low regime conviction tends to misprice both duration and credit simultaneously.

The single reading that flips the stance is a regime score rising above 50 paired with the bearish pair count falling from 15. Until that happens, the contrarian signal is a sentiment gauge, not a structural clearance.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The macro regime reads INFLATIONARY at 30% confidence. That low confidence level is itself a signal: the system is detecting inflationary dynamics but cannot commit to them, which puts you in a regime actively resolving rather than one where the path is clear.

An inflationary regime favors real assets, short duration, and commodity exposure. At 30% confidence, executing that playbook carries real error risk if the classification shifts.

The contrarian score at 76 in a capitulation/inflation context suggests sentiment has already sold the inflationary risk trade hard. Watch whether regime confidence rises toward 50% or the TRANSITION state reasserts itself with a different label.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

The cross-asset divergence composite is ELEVATED, with 47.5% of 40 pairs diverging, 15 in a bearish direction against only 4 bullish. Divergence means assets that normally move in sync have stopped doing so; correlation drift measures how far each pair's relationship has shifted from its recent norm.

Mother Jaws at 100 is the maximum reading the composite can produce. The sharpest pair is AUD/JPY vs SPY, where correlation deepened from -0.52 to -0.88: the safe-haven dynamic in that pair is intensifying sharply.

SPY/RSP drifted from +0.52 to -0.18, meaning the S&P 500 and its equal-weight version are now moving against each other, which tells you concentrated buying in the largest stocks is masking a broad selloff. VIX/MOVE moved from +0.20 to +0.79: equity vol and bond vol are now co-moving, a pattern that emerges when a macro repricing event spreads across asset classes.

Regional banks (KRE) vs broad financials (XLF) drifted from +0.11 to -0.58, signaling fractures inside the financial sector itself. Visa vs Mastercard drifted from +0.46 to -0.62: two stocks that almost always trade as a pair are now moving apart, pointing to fundamental repricing inside payments.

Asia · Europe · US · Crypto 24/7 — lead-lag detection
Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Every region is red over five days, but the dispersion in losses tells you where the pressure is concentrated. Korea (KOSPI, -4.4%) is the worst performer globally: it exports to both China and the US, and underperformance at this magnitude is pricing slower global goods demand.

The Russell 2000 at -3.0% is the US analog: small caps absorb the credit and rate sensitivity that large caps are shielded from by balance sheet quality. SSMI at -2.8% underperforms FTSE at -1.2% in Europe, reflecting greater rate sensitivity in the Swiss index versus UK defensives.

Crypto is not decorrelating: BTC at -1.2% and SOL at -1.6% are both tracking equity risk, with no safe-haven bid present. The consistent pattern across all four regions is rotation away from high-beta and cyclical exposure toward larger-cap, lower-volatility equity.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 1 out of 10 says realized price dislocations are minimal. VIX Spike sits at Tier 1 out of 4 with a 50% probability estimate and active skew, but no backwardation.

These two readings are coherent. The Crash Index measures what prices have already done.

The active skew flag measures what the options market is paying for going forward. Skew active without backwardation means dealers are pricing downside protection at a premium but are not yet inverting the futures curve.

You have early-stage hedging demand, not a full vol squeeze. Price is calm now; the options market is positioning for a vol expansion ahead.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.
Emerging industries: high velocity = screener scores accelerating this week vs prior baseline — potential early rotation signal.
Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
